messages:
riley: quick drop from today's design crit — focused on adaptive steppers + presets discoverability. prototype attached: https://figma.redwood/capacity-adaptive :eyes:
noor: good session. main worry: users don't realize step increments change with larger pools. propose an always-visible mini-hint: 'step: +1/+5/+10' next to steppers
diego: alternative: show a small badge that updates when you cross the threshold (e.g., 'step now +5'). less visual clutter at small sizes
shay: presets: want them accessible but not intrusive. idea: lightweight pill list above controls with a tiny cost delta microbadge and a help icon that opens inline explanation (no full page nav)
riley: love inline explainers. also add 'explain mode' toggle that overlays one-line helpers on hover/focus for each control. keyboard-accessible toggle too
noor: accessibility: color alone used for pool status in current mock. requirement: text-first badges, high-contrast strokes, and screen-reader label e.g., 'A100 40GB — 12 available'
diego: burst copy confusion persists. propose: label 'Burst window (mins)' and secondary caption: 'temporary extra GPUs (example: +2 GPUs for 20 mins)'. helps set expectation
shay: UX microflow: when a preset is applied, show an inline diff row with per-field tiny revert buttons, and a toast: 'Preset applied — undo?' for 10s. clicking revert restores previous values client-side before server confirm
noor: keyboard behavior: '/' focuses pool search. arrows navigate presets. Enter applies preset. Stepper keyboard acceleration: hold Shift to multiply step by 5, hold Alt to multiply by 10 (announce multiplier in tooltip)
riley: tiny dev note for infra (for simulate endpoint):
```
POST /api/v1/capacity/simulate
{ "pool_id": "pool-9x", "min": 4, "max": 20, "burst_minutes": 30 }
```
response: { "cost_delta_bucket": "small", "quota_status": "near", "tail95_ms": 160 }

noor: UI: simulator panel as collapsible right rail. on mobile collapse to single summary row with copyable quick-share link for support tickets
diego: analytics: instrument preset_impression, preset_apply, stepper_hold_accelerated, simulator_toggle, undo_click. we'll A/B test 'presets-inline' vs 'presets-sidebar' to measure confusion/support hits
shay: guardrail language: soften to avoid scaring users. suggested: "This change may approach your quota. Applying will request capacity and could affect billing. Request increase" (inline CTA)
ux-bot: generated updated frames 1809991300  https://figma.redwood/flow/1809991300 :white_check_mark:
riley: final asks: 1) show adaptive-step hint (text) near steppers 2) presets as lightweight pills with cost microbadge + inline explain 3) explain-mode toggle + keyboard access 4) inline diffs + per-field revert + undo toast 5) pool badges text-first and accessible 6) simulator right-rail collapsed on mobile 7) A/B test flag for presets placement
noor: i'll run accessibility checklist once frames land. diego please coordinate simulate endpoint with infra-bot
diego: noted. infra-bot: can we include cost_delta_bucket (small/medium/large) in simulate response and a prefilled request_increase_url when quota_status != ok?
infra-bot: yes. we'll add cost_delta_bucket and request_increase_url to the simulate payload response. planning ETA: 3 days
riley: thanks team 680. tagging eng & analytics. closing thread after assets exported."
